title: Migrate Node loadgen to Rust runner to improve stability and memory profile
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our existing Node-based synthetic load generator has become a recurring source of CI flakes, out-of-memory incidents on long-running perf regressions, and large tail-latency variance when running high-concurrency scenarios. The Node runner also pulls heavy JS dependencies, complicates reproducible builds, and makes native integrations (Python/Go) awkward. Goal: Replace the Node loadgen with a memory-safe Rust runner that preserves existing scenario semantics, improves 99th-percentile stability, and reduces memory footprint and GC-induced latency spikes. The new runner should be an opinionated, embeddable binary with a small FFI footprint so other tools (Python harnesses, CI agents) can invoke it reliably.
acceptance_criteria: Rust runner reproduces current scenario YAML semantics with >=99% parity on token distribution and request sequencing
End-to-end nightly perf regression job shows at least 30% reduction in OOM incidents and 15-30% lower 99th-percentile latency variance compared to Node baseline
New runner emits the same Prometheus-compatible metrics and tracing spans so dashboards and alerting remain unchanged
CI integration: all perf regression PRs pass on the new runner in the perf-harness pipeline for 7 consecutive runs
Documentation and migration guide published (CONFLUENCE link) and at least two internal teams have validated the runner in staging
implementation_notes: Language/runtime: Tokio + Hyper + async-trait for stable async load generation
Scenario compatibility: implement a strict YAML->internal AST translator to ensure deterministic seeding and legacy option support
KV cache / prefix optimization: keep behavior identical to Node implementation; add unit tests that compare token-level outputs for canonical scenarios
Bindings: provide a small gRPC shim for remote orchestration and a C-compatible FFI for direct embed in Python/Go test runners
CI: add a lightweight Docker image (redwood/loadgen-rust:canary) and smoke tests for startup/shutdown behaviour
Telemetry: push metrics via StatsD/Prometheus and include structured log lines for trace-id correlation
Security: runner will run non-privileged; ensure no arbitrary exec and validate scenario inputs before execution
testing_plan: Unit tests for scenario parser and deterministic seeding (target 90% coverage on parser module)
Cross-runner parity tests: compare Node vs Rust outputs for 20 canonical scenarios and flag diffs >0.5% token divergence
Memory-pressure CI job: run long-lived regression at 100 concurrent connections for 6 hours to validate no memory leak
Canary rollout: run subset of nightly jobs on Rust runner and compare traces and metrics before full cutover
Load validation with GPU-backed model endpoints to exercise real serialization and KV cache hot paths
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Canary: Deploy Rust runner image to perf CI pool and run against non-critical nightly suites for 2 weeks
Phase 2 - Parallel: Add option in perf pipeline to run both Node and Rust for same scenarios; require parity checks to be green
Phase 3 - Cutover: Switch default executor to Rust for all perf jobs once parity and stability thresholds are met
Phase 4 - Deprecate: Mark Node runner deprecated, create follow-up ticket to remove Node code and update docs
risks: Tokenization or timing differences cause hard-to-detect output divergence in certain stochastic scenarios
Embedding FFI surface introduces platform-specific issues on older CI images
Unforeseen perf regressions in extreme-high-concurrency cases due to scheduler interaction
Operational friction: teams used to Node debugging will need runbooks and tooling updates
